title: Modified anisotropy and distinct phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$
authors: Xuejuan Gui, Xu-Guang Zhou, Chen Zhang, Zhongcen Sun, Yuan Sun, Chenglin Shang, Akira Matsuo, Yasuhiro H. Matsuda, Koichi Kindo, Henrik M. Rønnow, Weiqiang Yu, Rong Yu, Peng Cheng, Juanjuan Liu, Jieming Sheng, Jinchen Wang
abstract: The triangular-lattice antiferromagnet serves as a benchmark platform for realizing exotic quantum phases, in which magnetic anisotropy plays an essential role. In this work, we report modified magnetic anisotropy and phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$, compared with those of its isostructural analog $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The magnetic susceptibility of $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ exhibits an easy-axis anisotropy with $g_c > g_{ab}$, opposite to the easy-plane anisotropy observed in $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The single Néel transition observed at zero field splits into two transitions at around 10~T, and a magnetization plateau is observed between 21~T and 37~T for both out-of-plane ($H\parallel c$) and in-plane ($H\parallel ab$) field directions in $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. We construct magnetic phase diagrams that are distinct between $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ and $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. These findings highlight the sensitivity of field-induced magnetic phase behavior to anisotropy in nearly isotropic triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.
summary: This work experimentally characterizes the magnetic anisotropy and phase diagram of the S=1 triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Rb2Ni(SeO3)2. By comparing it to a related compound, the authors demonstrate that the magnetic response is strongly dictated by the type of anisotropy, revealing distinct high-field transitions and magnetization plateaus. These findings underscore the critical role of anisotropy in determining exotic quantum magnetic phases.
main_problem: The study investigates the modified magnetic anisotropy and resulting distinct magnetic phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic S=1 triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Rb2Ni(SeO3)2.
main_result: The material exhibits easy-axis anisotropy (opposite to its analog K2Ni(SeO3)2), leading to a split Néel transition at high fields and distinct magnetization plateaus in both field directions.
method: The research combines single-crystal X-ray diffraction, magnetic susceptibility measurements, and pulsed high-field magnetization measurements up to 60 T.
model_or_system: The system is the S=1 triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Rb2Ni(SeO3)2, which is quasi-two-dimensional. The magnetic behavior is governed by the interplay between exchange anisotropy (Delta) and single-ion anisotropy (D).
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), Néel temperature ($T_N$), magnetization plateaus (e.g., 21 T to 37 T), and the anisotropy ratio $\chi_c / \chi_{ab}$.
important_parameters: The anisotropy strength (easy-axis vs. easy-plane), the applied magnetic field strength (up to 60 T), and the temperature (e.g., 4.2 K).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the magnetic phase behavior is highly sensitive to the relative strengths of single-ion and exchange anisotropies.
figures_summary: Figures show X-ray diffraction data, temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) for different field orientations, and pulsed high-field magnetization ($M$ vs $H$) curves demonstrating plateaus and split transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the magnetic properties of Rb2Ni(SeO3)2 to its analog K2Ni(SeO3)2, detailing anisotropy measurements, high-field magnetization studies, and constructing distinct magnetic phase diagrams based on these experimental findings.
why_interesting: The detailed study of field-induced phase transitions and the explicit role of competing anisotropies (single-ion vs. exchange) in a quasi-2D magnetic system is highly relevant to understanding quantum magnetism in correlated materials.
